title: Resolve customer escalation: maintenance-induced scheduler drift causing multi-mode continuous-batcher starvation
creator: Rohit Singh
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported sustained long-context tail latency and short-request starvation coincident with control-plane maintenance windows. Triage shows a cascade: maintenance quiesce triggers scheduler lease refresh across hosts, which interacts poorly with the continuous-batcher prefetch/kv-cache eviction logic and per-tenant admission fencing, producing eviction waves and effective queue starvation for short requests. This ticket tracks the triage, mitigation, root-cause fix, and rollout.

Reproduction (observed):
- Occurs after a coordinator maintenance window or private upgrade quiesce (seen consistently in private customer A and hosted us-west1 maintenance).
- Timeline: maintenance triggers lease rotation -> scheduler snapshotting stalls for ~150-400ms on some hosts -> continuous-batcher prefetch handshake times out -> KV cache eviction triggered for long inflight sequences -> admission window shrinks for short requests -> small requests queue up and see high tail latency while long-context flows continue.

Affected surfaces: Hosted API (us-west1), Dedicated pools with mixed tenant workloads, and Private on-prem upgrades when maintenance-quiesce handshake is used.

Root cause hypothesis: The maintenance quiesce handshake sets a per-host scheduler fence timeout that races with the continuous-batcher's prefetch handshake. When the fence extends (due to coordinator GC/DB latency), prefetch paths clear cached reservation tokens and trigger eviction hysteresis. The eviction path currently lacks a 'grace reanchor' for in-flight small-request reservation tokens, so admission accounting permanently undercounts short flows until a full token refresh.

Why existing fixes missed this: Prior work focused on admission-window fairness and prefetch quarantine but assumed fence lifetimes were bounded by the coordinator. Here the fence lifetime can be extended by unrelated maintenance tasks (upgrade/unmount) leading to prolonged token invalidation and unexpected eviction waves across hosting modes.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix deployed and validated in canary hosts: no repeated tail-latency spikes for short requests during simulated maintenance windows
Root-cause patch merges to main runtime and passes unit + e2e tests under simulated lease rotations
Rollout plan documented and approved by SRE and Product; rollback toggle available
Customer-facing incidents closed with post-mortem and follow-up action items assigned
plan: Phase 0 - Mitigation (hotfix): introduce 'admission grace token' that persists short-request reservations across transient fence expansions; deploy as feature-flagged change to runtime hosts
Phase 1 - Patch: implement 'quiesce handshake awareness' in continuous-batcher so prefetch does not clear reservation tokens when scheduler fence extends; add eviction hysteresis backstop
Phase 2 - Testing: unit tests for token lifecycle, integration test simulating coordinator GC-induced fence extension, chaos test under mixed-hosting workload
Phase 3 - Canary: 10% canary on hosted us-west1 and one Dedicated pool (customer-sim cluster), plus private customer A test cluster; monitor for 72h
Phase 4 - Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regions and private customers with 1-hour observation gates
Phase 5 - Post-mortem: finalize incident report, update runbooks and maintenance guidance for Private upgrades
telemetry_checks: Dashboard: /dashboards/continuous-batcher/tail-latency-by-tenant (check p95/p99 for short-request tag before/after maintenance)
Query: SUM(rate(eviction_events[5m])) by host -> alert if > 5x baseline during maintenance window
Query: increase in 'admission_undercount' metric correlating with coordinator_fence_extend_count
Canary alarm: p99(latency{request_type="short"}) > 200ms for more than 2 consecutive 5m buckets
